# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
PipeQueue::undo
Summary: Re-inserts the supplied pipe at the front of the queue, allowing
         the player to reuse a pipe that was just undone.
Algorithm:
  1. Insert the supplied pipe at index 0 of pipeQueue, shifting existing
     elements back by one.
Related Features: pipeQueue : List<Pipe>.
Related Classes: Pipe.
Input: pipe : Pipe — the pipe to be returned to the head of the queue.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: pipe is non-null.
Post-condition: pipe is now the head element; the queue size is increased
               by 1. If the queue exceeds maxGenLength, no trimming is
               performed (the undo is permissive).

PipeQueue::consume
Summary: Removes the head pipe from the queue, simulating the player using
         the current pipe either by placing it or by skipping it.
Algorithm:
  1. Remove and discard pipeQueue[0] (the head element).
  2. If the queue's size has dropped below maxGenLength, append a newly
     generated pipe via generateNewPipe() to keep the queue topped up.
Related Features: pipeQueue : List<Pipe>, maxGenLength : int.
Related Classes: Pipe.
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The queue is non-empty.
Post-condition: The previous head pipe is gone; the queue length is at
               least maxGenLength - 1, and is automatically refilled.

PipeQueue::generateNewPipe
Summary: Creates a new random Pipe instance for refilling the queue.
Algorithm:
  1. Pick a random PipeShape value from the seven supported shapes
     (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT,
     CROSS) with uniform probability.
  2. Construct a new Pipe with that shape and a default unfilled state.
  3. Return the pipe.
Related Features: maxGenLength : int.
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape.
Input: None.
Output: Pipe — a freshly constructed pipe with an unfilled state and a
        random shape.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: A new Pipe object exists; the queue state is unchanged by
               this method alone (caller is responsible for inserting it).

PipeQueue::peek
Summary: Returns the head pipe of the queue without removing it. The
         returned pipe is the one the player will place or skip next.
Algorithm:
  1. If pipeQueue is empty, return null.
  2. Otherwise, return pipeQueue[0].
Related Features: pipeQueue : List<Pipe>.
Related Classes: Pipe.
Input: None.
Output: Pipe — the pipe at the front of the queue, or null if empty.
Pre-condition: The queue may be empty.
Post-condition: The queue is unchanged.

  3. Return the pipe.
Related Features: maxGenLength : int.
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape.
Input: None.
Output: Pipe — a freshly constructed pipe with an unfilled state and a
        random shape.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: A new Pipe object exists; the queue state is unchanged by
               this method alone (caller is responsible for inserting it).

PipeQueue::peek
Summary: Returns the head pipe of the queue without removing it. The
         returned pipe is the one the player will place or skip next.
Algorithm:
  1. If pipeQueue is empty, return null.
  2. Otherwise, return pipeQueue[0].
Related Features: pipeQueue : List<Pipe>.
Related Classes: Pipe.
Input: None.
Output: Pipe — the pipe at the front of the queue, or null if empty.
Pre-condition: The queue may be empty.
Post-condition: The queue is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
CellStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the most recently placed FillableCell from the
         top of the stack. Used by Game.undoStep to revert a placement.
Algorithm:
  1. If the internal stack is empty, return null (or throw an exception —
     inferred defensive behavior).
  2. Remove the last element from the stack list.
  3. Increment the count field to record this successful undo.
  4. Return the removed FillableCell.
Related Features: stack : List<FillableCell>, count : int.
Related Classes: FillableCell.
Input: None.
Output: FillableCell — the most recently pushed cell, or null if the stack
        is empty.
Pre-condition: The stack has been previously populated via push(); if the
               stack is empty, behavior is to return null.
Post-condition: The returned cell is removed from the stack list and the
               undo counter is incremented by exactly 1.

CellStack::getUndoCount
Summary: Returns the number of successful undo actions that have been performed
         on this stack. The counter tracks completed pop operations and is
         independent of the current stack size.
Algorithm:
  1. Return the value of the internal count field.
Related Features: count : int (the running tally of successful pop operations).
Related Classes: None.
Input: None.
Output: int — the number of successful undo (pop) operations recorded so far,
        in the range [0, +∞).
Pre-condition: The CellStack object must be properly constructed.
Post-condition: The state of the CellStack is not modified; the value of the
               count field is returned unchanged.

CellStack::push
Summary: Appends a FillableCell to the top of the stack so that it can be
         reverted later by pop(). Invoked whenever Game places a pipe.
Algorithm:
  1. Add the given FillableCell to the end of the internal stack list.
Related Features: stack : List<FillableCell>.
Related Classes: FillableCell.
Input: cell : FillableCell — the cell that was just occupied by a pipe.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The supplied cell is non-null and represents a successfully
               placed pipe position.
Post-condition: The cell is recorded as the most recent placement and will
               be the next item returned by pop().

# Operation Specifications
CellStack::pop
Summary: Removes and returns the most recently placed FillableCell from the
         top of the stack. Used by Game.undoStep to revert a placement.
Algorithm:
  1. If the internal stack is empty, return null (or throw an exception —
     inferred defensive behavior).
  2. Remove the last element from the stack list.
  3. Increment the count field to record this successful undo.
  4. Return the removed FillableCell.
Related Features: stack : List<FillableCell>, count : int.
Related Classes: FillableCell.
Input: None.
Output: FillableCell — the most recently pushed cell, or null if the stack
        is empty.
Pre-condition: The stack has been previously populated via push(); if the
               stack is empty, behavior is to return null.
Post-condition: The returned cell is removed from the stack list and the
               undo counter is incremented by exactly 1.

CellStack::getUndoCount
Summary: Returns the number of successful undo actions that have been performed
         on this stack. The counter tracks completed pop operations and is
         independent of the current stack size.
Algorithm:
  1. Return the value of the internal count field.
Related Features: count : int (the running tally of successful pop operations).
Related Classes: None.
Input: None.
Output: int — the number of successful undo (pop) operations recorded so far,
        in the range [0, +∞).
Pre-condition: The CellStack object must be properly constructed.
Post-condition: The state of the CellStack is not modified; the value of the
               count field is returned unchanged.

CellStack::push
Summary: Appends a FillableCell to the top of the stack so that it can be
         reverted later by pop(). Invoked whenever Game places a pipe.
Algorithm:
  1. Add the given FillableCell to the end of the internal stack list.
Related Features: stack : List<FillableCell>.
Related Classes: FillableCell.
Input: cell : FillableCell — the cell that was just occupied by a pipe.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The supplied cell is non-null and represents a successfully
               placed pipe position.
Post-condition: The cell is recorded as the most recent placement and will
               be the next item returned by pop().

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::skipPipe
Summary: Discards the head pipe from the queue without placing it and
         increments the step counter.
Algorithm:
  1. Call pipeQueue.consume() to drop the head pipe.
  2. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, pipeQueue : PipeQueue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue.
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The pipe queue is non-empty.
Post-condition: The previous head pipe is removed from the queue and the
               step counter is increased by 1. The map is unchanged.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Reverts the most recent successful pipe placement, restoring the
         pipe to the head of the queue and clearing the cell on the map.
         Returns false when there is nothing to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop(); if it returns null, return false (no history).
  2. From the popped FillableCell, recover its coordinate.
  3. Call map.undo(coord) to clear that cell on the map.
  4. Take the pipe from the popped cell and call pipeQueue.undo(pipe) to
     reinsert it at the head of the queue.
  5. Increment numOfSteps.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, cellStack : CellStack, pipeQueue : PipeQueue,
                  map : Map.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if an undo was performed, false when the stack is
        empty.
Pre-condition: A previous successful placePipe() has occurred; otherwise
               the call returns false without side effects.
Post-condition: The map cell previously occupied by the latest pipe is
               cleared, the pipe is returned to the head of the queue, and
               numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the player has lost the current round. A loss
         occurs when the most recent water-flow round failed to fill any
         additional pipe, meaning the water path is blocked.
Algorithm:
  1. If the water-flow delay has not finished (i.e., distance is still
     negative), return false.
  2. Otherwise, delegate to Map.hasLost() and return its result.
Related Features: map : Map, delayBar : DelayBar.
Related Classes: Map.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if the game is in a loss state, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Game is fully constructed and at least one updateState()
               has been executed (so prevFilledTiles is meaningful).
Post-condition: The game state is not modified.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Places the head pipe from the queue at the location selected by
         the player, expressed as a row number and a column letter. The
         step counter is incremented on a successful placement.
Algorithm:
  1. Translate the player-supplied column letter to an internal column
     index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Obtain the head pipe by calling pipeQueue.peek().
  3. Invoke map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, headPipe).
  4. If placement succeeds:
       a. Push the affected FillableCell onto cellStack so it can be undone.
       b. Advance the queue by calling pipeQueue.consume().
       c. Increment numOfSteps.
       d. Return true.
  5. Otherwise, return false (invalid coordinates or occupied cell).
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, cellStack : CellStack, pipeQueue : PipeQueue,
                  map : Map.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, FillableCell, Pipe.
Input:
  row : int — the player-facing row number in [1, rows-2] (playable range).
  col : char — a column letter from 'A'..(A + cols-3) inclusive; mapped to
               [1, cols-2] via col - 'A' + 1.
Output: boolean — true if the pipe was placed successfully, false if the
        target cell is out of range or already occupied.
Pre-condition: The row is within the playable range; the column letter is a
               valid map character; the queue is non-empty.
Post-condition: On success, the head pipe is consumed from the queue, the
               cell contains the pipe, cellStack records the placement, and
               numOfSteps is increased by 1. On failure, no state changes.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Reports whether the player has connected the source to the sink
         by placing pipes that form a valid path.
Algorithm:
  1. Delegate to Map.checkPath() and return its boolean result.
Related Features: map : Map.
Related Classes: Map.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if a connected path from SOURCE to SINK exists.
Pre-condition: Game is fully constructed with a valid source and sink.
Post-condition: The game state is not modified.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game simulation by one round, triggering the delay
         countdown and the water-flow propagation on the map.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown() to advance the delay by one tick.
  2. Compute d = delayBar.distance().
  3. If d > 0 (delay has ended and water should flow):
       a. Call map.fillTiles(d) to propagate water along connected pipes.
  4. Otherwise, ensure the source is marked as filled by calling
     map.fillBeginTile() (so the SOURCE cell always appears filled).
  5. (Implicit) Update prevFilledTiles on the map for the next loss check.
Related Features: delayBar : DelayBar, map : Map, cellStack : CellStack.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map.
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The game is fully constructed; called once per round by the
               game loop.
Post-condition: DelayBar has advanced, the SOURCE cell is filled, and the
               water flow has been propagated d steps along reachable pipes.

  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

# Operation Specifications
Game::skipPipe
Summary: Discards the head pipe from the queue without placing it and
         increments the step counter.
Algorithm:
  1. Call pipeQueue.consume() to drop the head pipe.
  2. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, pipeQueue : PipeQueue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue.
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The pipe queue is non-empty.
Post-condition: The previous head pipe is removed from the queue and the
               step counter is increased by 1. The map is unchanged.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Reverts the most recent successful pipe placement, restoring the
         pipe to the head of the queue and clearing the cell on the map.
         Returns false when there is nothing to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop(); if it returns null, return false (no history).
  2. From the popped FillableCell, recover its coordinate.
  3. Call map.undo(coord) to clear that cell on the map.
  4. Take the pipe from the popped cell and call pipeQueue.undo(pipe) to
     reinsert it at the head of the queue.
  5. Increment numOfSteps.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, cellStack : CellStack, pipeQueue : PipeQueue,
                  map : Map.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if an undo was performed, false when the stack is
        empty.
Pre-condition: A previous successful placePipe() has occurred; otherwise
               the call returns false without side effects.
Post-condition: The map cell previously occupied by the latest pipe is
               cleared, the pipe is returned to the head of the queue, and
               numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the player has lost the current round. A loss
         occurs when the most recent water-flow round failed to fill any
         additional pipe, meaning the water path is blocked.
Algorithm:
  1. If the water-flow delay has not finished (i.e., distance is still
     negative), return false.
  2. Otherwise, delegate to Map.hasLost() and return its result.
Related Features: map : Map, delayBar : DelayBar.
Related Classes: Map.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if the game is in a loss state, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Game is fully constructed and at least one updateState()
               has been executed (so prevFilledTiles is meaningful).
Post-condition: The game state is not modified.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Places the head pipe from the queue at the location selected by
         the player, expressed as a row number and a column letter. The
         step counter is incremented on a successful placement.
Algorithm:
  1. Translate the player-supplied column letter to an internal column
     index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Obtain the head pipe by calling pipeQueue.peek().
  3. Invoke map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, headPipe).
  4. If placement succeeds:
       a. Push the affected FillableCell onto cellStack so it can be undone.
       b. Advance the queue by calling pipeQueue.consume().
       c. Increment numOfSteps.
       d. Return true.
  5. Otherwise, return false (invalid coordinates or occupied cell).
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, cellStack : CellStack, pipeQueue : PipeQueue,
                  map : Map.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, FillableCell, Pipe.
Input:
  row : int — the player-facing row number in [1, rows-2] (playable range).
  col : char — a column letter from 'A'..(A + cols-3) inclusive; mapped to
               [1, cols-2] via col - 'A' + 1.
Output: boolean — true if the pipe was placed successfully, false if the
        target cell is out of range or already occupied.
Pre-condition: The row is within the playable range; the column letter is a
               valid map character; the queue is non-empty.
Post-condition: On success, the head pipe is consumed from the queue, the
               cell contains the pipe, cellStack records the placement, and
               numOfSteps is increased by 1. On failure, no state changes.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Reports whether the player has connected the source to the sink
         by placing pipes that form a valid path.
Algorithm:
  1. Delegate to Map.checkPath() and return its boolean result.
Related Features: map : Map.
Related Classes: Map.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if a connected path from SOURCE to SINK exists.
Pre-condition: Game is fully constructed with a valid source and sink.
Post-condition: The game state is not modified.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game simulation by one round, triggering the delay
         countdown and the water-flow propagation on the map.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown() to advance the delay by one tick.
  2. Compute d = delayBar.distance().
  3. If d > 0 (delay has ended and water should flow):
       a. Call map.fillTiles(d) to propagate water along connected pipes.
  4. Otherwise, ensure the source is marked as filled by calling
     map.fillBeginTile() (so the SOURCE cell always appears filled).
  5. (Implicit) Update prevFilledTiles on the map for the next loss check.
Related Features: delayBar : DelayBar, map : Map, cellStack : CellStack.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map.
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The game is fully constructed; called once per round by the
               game loop.
Post-condition: DelayBar has advanced, the SOURCE cell is filled, and the
               water flow has been propagated d steps along reachable pipes.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by

  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.

  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short

# Operation Specifications
Game::skipPipe
Summary: Discards the head pipe from the queue without placing it and
         increments the step counter.
Algorithm:
  1. Call pipeQueue.consume() to drop the head pipe.
  2. Increment numOfSteps by 1.
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, pipeQueue : PipeQueue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue.
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The pipe queue is non-empty.
Post-condition: The previous head pipe is removed from the queue and the
               step counter is increased by 1. The map is unchanged.

Game::undoStep
Summary: Reverts the most recent successful pipe placement, restoring the
         pipe to the head of the queue and clearing the cell on the map.
         Returns false when there is nothing to undo.
Algorithm:
  1. Call cellStack.pop(); if it returns null, return false (no history).
  2. From the popped FillableCell, recover its coordinate.
  3. Call map.undo(coord) to clear that cell on the map.
  4. Take the pipe from the popped cell and call pipeQueue.undo(pipe) to
     reinsert it at the head of the queue.
  5. Increment numOfSteps.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, cellStack : CellStack, pipeQueue : PipeQueue,
                  map : Map.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if an undo was performed, false when the stack is
        empty.
Pre-condition: A previous successful placePipe() has occurred; otherwise
               the call returns false without side effects.
Post-condition: The map cell previously occupied by the latest pipe is
               cleared, the pipe is returned to the head of the queue, and
               numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the player has lost the current round. A loss
         occurs when the most recent water-flow round failed to fill any
         additional pipe, meaning the water path is blocked.
Algorithm:
  1. If the water-flow delay has not finished (i.e., distance is still
     negative), return false.
  2. Otherwise, delegate to Map.hasLost() and return its result.
Related Features: map : Map, delayBar : DelayBar.
Related Classes: Map.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if the game is in a loss state, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The game is fully constructed; the loss check is only
               meaningful after the delay has ended (distance > 0);
               otherwise the method returns false without consulting
               the map.
Post-condition: The game state is not modified.

Game::placePipe
Summary: Places the head pipe from the queue at the location selected by
         the player, expressed as a row number and a column letter. The
         step counter is incremented on a successful placement.
Algorithm:
  1. Translate the player-supplied column letter to an internal column
     index: colIndex = col - 'A' + 1.
  2. Obtain the head pipe by calling pipeQueue.peek().
  3. Invoke map.tryPlacePipe(row, colIndex, headPipe).
  4. If placement succeeds:
       a. Push the affected FillableCell onto cellStack so it can be undone.
       b. Advance the queue by calling pipeQueue.consume().
       c. Increment numOfSteps.
       d. Return true.
  5. Otherwise, return false (invalid coordinates or occupied cell).
Related Features: numOfSteps : int, cellStack : CellStack, pipeQueue : PipeQueue,
                  map : Map.
Related Classes: Map, PipeQueue, CellStack, FillableCell, Pipe.
Input:
  row : int — the player-facing row number in [1, rows-2] (playable range).
  col : char — a column letter from 'A'..(A + cols-3) inclusive; mapped to
               [1, cols-2] via col - 'A' + 1.
Output: boolean — true if the pipe was placed successfully, false if the
        target cell is out of range or already occupied.
Pre-condition: The row is within the playable range; the column letter is a
               valid map character; the queue is non-empty.
Post-condition: On success, the head pipe is consumed from the queue, the
               cell contains the pipe, cellStack records the placement, and
               numOfSteps is increased by 1. On failure, no state changes.

Game::hasWon
Summary: Reports whether the player has connected the source to the sink
         by placing pipes that form a valid path.
Algorithm:
  1. Delegate to Map.checkPath() and return its boolean result.
Related Features: map : Map.
Related Classes: Map.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true if a connected path from SOURCE to SINK exists.
Pre-condition: Game is fully constructed with a valid source and sink.
Post-condition: The game state is not modified.

Game::updateState
Summary: Advances the game simulation by one round, triggering the delay
         countdown and the water-flow propagation on the map.
Algorithm:
  1. Call delayBar.countdown() to advance the delay by one tick.
  2. Compute d = delayBar.distance().
  3. If d > 0 (delay has ended and water should flow):
       a. Call map.fillTiles(d) to propagate water along connected pipes.
  4. Otherwise, ensure the source is marked as filled by calling
     map.fillBeginTile() (so the SOURCE cell always appears filled).
  5. After fillTiles (when d > 0), the map's prevFilledTiles and
     prevFilledDistance are updated internally so that hasLost() can
     detect whether any new tiles were filled this round.
Related Features: delayBar : DelayBar, map : Map.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map.
Input: None.
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The game is fully constructed; called once per round by the
               game loop.
Post-condition: DelayBar has advanced by one tick; the SOURCE cell is
                filled; and water has been propagated d steps along
                reachable pipes (when d > 0). The map records
                prevFilledTiles / prevFilledDistance for the next loss
                check.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary: Attempts to place a pipe at the given playable-area coordinates.
         Coordinates are used directly as array indices (no row-1/col-1
         conversion) because the outer walls occupy index 0 and rows-1/cols-1.
Algorithm:
  1. Reject (return false) if row is outside [1, rows-2] or col is outside
     [1, cols-2].
  2. Reject (return false) if cells[row][col] is not a FillableCell
     (e.g., a Wall or TerminationCell).
  3. Reject (return false) if the cell is already occupied by a pipe.
  4. Otherwise, cast the cell to FillableCell, set its pipe field, and
     return true.
Related Features: cell : Cell[][], rows : int, cols : int.
Related Classes: Cell, FillableCell, Pipe.
Input:
  row : int — internal array row in [1, rows-2].
  col : int — internal array col in [1, cols-2].
  pipe : Pipe — the pipe object to install.
Output: boolean — true on success, false on any rejection reason.
Pre-condition: The map has been constructed with a border of walls and the
               inner cells are FillableCells.
Post-condition: On success, cells[row][col] now references the supplied pipe
               via its FillableCell.pipe field. On failure, the map is
               unchanged.

Map::fillTiles
Summary: Propagates water outward from the SOURCE using a BFS-style
         expansion that fills any pipe cell whose connection to a
         already-filled neighbour matches (i.e., one pipe's direction is
         the opposite of its neighbour's).
Algorithm:
  1. Reset the working frontier and pre-allocate a new filledTiles list.
  2. Push the source cell as the initial frontier (BFS seed).
  3. For each cell in the frontier, examine its four neighbours within
     the playable area.
  4. For each neighbour:
       a. If neighbour is unfilled and holds a pipe whose connections
          include a direction opposite to the direction from the current
          cell, and the current cell's connections include the matching
          direction, mark the neighbour as filled and add it to the next
          frontier.
  5. Repeat the expansion until no more cells are filled or the distance
     budget is exhausted.
  6. Update prevFilledTiles to the number of newly filled cells in this
     round and update prevFilledDistance.
Related Features: cell : Cell[][], filledTiles : List<Coordinate>,
                  prevFilledTiles : int, prevFilledDistance, sourceCell,
                  sinkCell.
Related Classes: Cell, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, Coordinate, Pa19Helper
                  (for getOpposite and getOffset).
Input: distance : int — the number of BFS layers to expand from the source.
                     Typically the positive result of DelayBar.distance().
Output: void.
Pre-condition: fillBeginTile() has been called so the source is marked
               filled; the map has been constructed with a valid source cell.
Post-condition: All reachable pipes within `distance` BFS layers are marked
               as filled; prevFilledTiles and prevFilledDistance are updated
               for the subsequent loss check.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the most recent water-flow round failed to fill
         any new pipe cells.
Algorithm:
  1. Return (prevFilledTiles == 0).
Related Features: prevFilledTiles : int.
Related Classes: None.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true when no pipes were filled during the previous
        round, indicating a loss.
Pre-condition: At least one fillTiles() call (with positive distance) has
               completed so that prevFilledTiles is meaningful.
Post-condition: The map state is unchanged.

Map::undo
Summary: Clears any pipe installed at the given coordinate, reverting the
         cell back to an empty FillableCell. Invoked by Game.undoStep.
Algorithm:
  1. Look up cells[coord.row][coord.col].
  2. If it is a FillableCell, set its pipe field to null.
  3. Ignore (or no-op) for non-fillable cells.
Related Features: cell : Cell[][].
Related Classes: Cell, FillableCell, Coordinate.
Input: coord : Coordinate — the internal-array coordinates of the cell
                   to clear; should be within [1, rows-2] × [1, cols-2].
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The coordinate points to a valid map cell.
Post-condition: The target FillableCell no longer holds a pipe; rendered
               character returns to '.'.

  3. Reject (return false) if the cell is already occupied by a pipe.
  4. Otherwise, cast the cell to FillableCell, set its pipe field, and

Related Features: cell : Cell[][], rows : int, cols : int.

  row : int — internal array row in [1, rows-2].
  col : int — internal array col in [1, cols-2].
  pipe : Pipe — the pipe object to install.

         expansion that fills any pipe cell whose connection to a
         already-filled neighbour matches (i.e., one pipe's direction is
         the opposite of its neighbour's).
Algorithm:
  1. Reset the working frontier and pre-allocate a new filledTiles list.
  2. Push the source cell as the initial frontier (BFS seed).
  3. For each cell in the frontier, examine its four neighbours within
     the playable area.
  4. For each neighbour:
       a. If neighbour is unfilled and holds a pipe whose connections
          include a direction opposite to the direction from the current
          cell, and the current cell's connections include the matching
          direction, mark the neighbour as filled and add it to the next
          frontier.
  5. Repeat the expansion until no more cells are filled or the distance
     budget is exhausted.
  6. Update prevFilledTiles to the number of newly filled cells in this
     round and update prevFilledDistance.
Related Features: cell : Cell[][], filledTiles : List<Coordinate>,
                  prevFilledTiles : int, prevFilledDistance, sourceCell,
                  sinkCell.
Related Classes: Cell, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, Coordinate, Pa19Helper
                  (for getOpposite and getOffset).
Input: distance : int — the number of BFS layers to expand from the source.
                     Typically the positive result of DelayBar.distance().
Output: void.
Pre-condition: fillBeginTile() has been called so the source is marked
               filled; the map has been constructed with a valid source cell.
Post-condition: All reachable pipes within `distance` BFS layers are marked
               as filled; prevFilledTiles and prevFilledDistance are updated
               for the subsequent loss check.

Map::hasLost
Summary: Reports whether the most recent water-flow round failed to fill
         any new pipe cells.
Algorithm:
  1. Return (prevFilledTiles == 0).
Related Features: prevFilledTiles : int.
Related Classes: None.
Input: None.
Output: boolean — true when no pipes were filled during the previous
        round, indicating a loss.
Pre-condition: At least one fillTiles() call (with positive distance) has
               completed so that prevFilledTiles is meaningful.
Post-condition: The map state is unchanged.

Map::undo
Summary: Clears any pipe installed at the given coordinate, reverting the
         cell back to an empty FillableCell. Invoked by Game.undoStep.
Algorithm:
  1. Look up cells[coord.row][coord.col].
  2. If it is a FillableCell, set its pipe field to null.
  3. Ignore (or no-op) for non-fillable cells.
Related Features: cell : Cell[][].
Related Classes: Cell, FillableCell, Coordinate.
Input: coord : Coordinate — the internal-array coordinates of the cell
                   to clear; should be within [1, rows-2] × [1, cols-2].
Output: void.
Pre-condition: The coordinate points to a valid map cell.
Post-condition: The target FillableCell no longer holds a pipe; rendered
               character returns to '.'.
